Senses.Explanation: The underlying scene is an ornate lock or fastening at palace halls and layered gates, not solid-gold hardware. Dadian Baotong says palace halls will not be closed with such locks when he returns to his mountain because white clouds will seal them by themselves. Zhuanyu Heng places the expression in a conventional ornate-palace sequence of jade steps, blue-green locked gates, layered gates, a precious glazed hall, and a jewel curtain. A parallel verse by Zhe'an Jingfan pairs jade palace gates with gold doors and ninefold gates. These controls establish ornate palace diction; they do not establish solid gold, gilding, gold color, an imperial code, or enlightenment symbolism. The records carry the same obstructing lock scene into the dominant Chan deployment at a pass or dark road. Yongjue Yuanxian calls an approving mind ‘the gold-lock dark road’ (只此肯心，便是金鎖玄路) and likewise says that ordinary feelings and holy views are that road (凡情聖見，是金鎖玄路). Baichi Yuan says even ‘the person with nothing going on’ remains a difficult lock (無為無事人，猶是金鎖難). Other records open or smash the lock-barrier, or call both hidden barrier and this lock expedient means that need opening. The Zen bend places approving mind, ordinary and holy views, and a seemingly unoccupied person behind the ornate barrier without turning the modifier into a material claim.
Senses.Note: The exact allowlisted concordance finds 349 string matches in 155 texts, including 45 longer yellow-gold-lock forms. Seventeen preliminary matches belong to distinct gold-chain-bone compounds, and nine further matches are nested gold-chain-link forms; they do not buy standalone depth. Across both senses, six standalone cards count toward depth, six longer-compound cards are marked family, and two palace-register controls are marked contrast. The architectural palace fastening supplies the ordinary pictured lock; the barrier compounds redeploy that same obstructing referent and therefore remain in one sense. Only the chain/fetter frames require a different object. The corpus-wide modifier study found material gold elsewhere, gold color, conventional epithets, local gold-refining comparisons, and a conventional ornate-palace register, but no equation that makes gold mean awakening or solid-gold construction here. The closest gold/silver comparison makes both complete compounds obstruction images rather than an awakening-versus-nonawakening code.

Occurrences.Kwic: 顛倒想滅，肯心自許。只此肯心，便是金鎖玄路，故有十劫觀樹之事。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yongjue Yuanxian, in his Extended Record (永覺元賢禪師廣錄), says that when inverted thinking has ceased and an approving mind certifies itself, just this approving mind is the gold-lock dark road.

Occurrences.Kwic: 凡情聖見，是金鎖玄路，故先聖以法淘汰之。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yongjue Yuanxian, in his Extended Record (永覺元賢禪師廣錄), says that ordinary feelings and holy views are the gold-lock dark road and that earlier sages therefore washed them away with the teaching.

Occurrences.Kwic: 直下劃開情塵見網，當陽擊碎金鎖玄關
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Baiyu Si, in the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baiyu (百愚禪師語錄), speaks of directly cutting open the net of feelings, dust, and views and openly smashing the gold-lock dark barrier.

Occurrences.Kwic: 金鎖玄關信手開，銀山鐵壁難遮截
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Weian Deran, in his Recorded Sayings (松隱唯菴然和尚語錄), says that the gold-lock dark barrier opens readily at hand and that the silver mountain and iron wall are unable to block or cut off. The paired silver image is a control, not a contrasting code for awakening.

Occurrences.Kwic: 玄關金鎖皆方便，只要當人薦得開。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Huangbo Wunian Shenyou, in the ‘Huangbo Wunian Further Questions’ section (黃蘗無念禪師復問) of the Record of Waking the Drowsy (黃蘗無念禪師醒昏錄), calls both the hidden barrier and ornate lock expedient means and says only that the person concerned must recognize how to open them.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雖然無為無事人，猶是金鎖難，且道：節角在什麼處？試下一轉語看。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Baichi Yuan, in the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baichi (百癡禪師語錄), repeats that even the person with nothing going on remains a difficult ornate lock-barrier, asks where the catch lies, and demands a turning word.

Occurrences.Kwic: 臺殿不將金鎖閉，來時自有白雲封。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dadian Baotong, in the Patriarchs’ Hall Collection (祖堂集) section headed ‘Preceptor Dadian’ (大顛和尚), says that the palace halls will not be shut with ornate palace locks when he returns; white clouds will seal them by themselves.

Occurrences.Kwic: 重門金鎖密難通，寶殿琉璃映日紅
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhuanyu Heng, in his Recorded Sayings at Purple Bamboo Grove (紫竹林顓愚衡和尚語錄), describes layered gates whose ornate lock makes them difficult to pass and a precious glazed palace reflecting the sun in red.

Occurrences.Kwic: 欲入普門深復深，九重深處更沉沉，玉階青鎖行人斷，寂寂簾垂鳥不音。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhuanyu Heng, in the same Universal Gate verses in his Purple Bamboo Grove record (紫竹林顓愚衡和尚語錄), first pictures jade steps and blue-green locked gates cutting off travelers, with a silent hanging curtain. This nearby color-and-ornament series controls how the later gold-lock line should be read.

Occurrences.Kwic: 玉闕金扉臥病人，綸音尤降九重門。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhean Jingfan, in the old-case verses of his Recorded Sayings (蔗菴範禪師語錄), pictures a sick person behind jade palace gates and gold doors while a formal decree descends through the ninefold gates. The paired modifiers establish conventional ornate-palace diction rather than solid-gold construction.

Senses.Explanation: A second corpus-wide image is a binding chain or animal fetter rather than a lock at a barrier. Its verbs require something that binds an animal and can be broken, pulled apart, or escaped. Baiyu Si pictures a soaring phoenix entangled in it (翀霄鸞鳳縈金鎖). Wuming Huijing speaks of a lion cub bursting it after an awakening exchange, but immediately says that both the exchange and this appraisal still incur fault. Baichi Yuan compares direct acceptance to an elephant-king pulling it apart and not turning back when called. Shiyu Mingfang’s inscription likewise places breaking it beside the movements of a fragrant elephant. These animal-and-binding frames establish a chain or fetter as a different object from the openable or smashable barrier-lock. The source still modifies the restraint with gold, but the corpus does not establish material composition or explain the modifier in these verses, so the displayed target names only the attested binding object.
Senses.Note: The split follows incompatible governing verbs and scenes, not two readings of one occurrence: a barrier-lock is opened, closed, pierced, or smashed at a pass; a chain or fetter entangles a flying bird and is escaped or pulled apart by a lion or elephant. Longer bone and relic compounds remain separate lexical objects. The adjective is classified as unresolved within this headword, while the complete animal-chain image is directly attested as figurative binding.

Occurrences.Kwic: 翀霄鸞鳳縈金鎖，挂角羺羊猶滯蹤
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Baiyu Si, in the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baiyu (百愚禪師語錄), writes that a phoenix soaring into the sky is entangled in a binding chain and that even the horn-hanging ram still leaves a trace.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧大悟，悟甚麼？獅兒迸斷黃金鎖。據實舉論，俱未免過。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Wuming Huijing, in his Recorded Sayings (壽昌無明和尚語錄), asks what the monk awakened to, says that a lion cub burst the binding chain, and then states that both still incur fault.

Occurrences.Kwic: 象王掣斷黃金鎖，呼喚竟不回頭。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Baichi Yuan, in the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baichi (百癡禪師語錄), says that the elephant-king pulls apart the binding chain and does not turn back when called.

Occurrences.Kwic: 登雲門堂，遐契於夙，擺壞金鎖，香象躑躅
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Shiyu Mingfang, in his Teaching Collection (石雨禪師法檀), writes in an inscription that after entering Yunmen’s hall and meeting an old affinity, the binding chain is broken and the fragrant elephant stamps ahead.
